findings.summary: Invariant (c) ('never an entrypoint, for any domain') now rests on the type's `category` field. Reclassify the interpreter as ENTRYPOINT, grant it to an unclosed domain, and nothing catches it. So the dropped A77.planeon_interpreter_exec_t was not unable to fail.
findings.evidence: Scratch two-op mutations on the round-5 matrix. Setting planeon_interpreter_exec_t's category to ENTRYPOINT and granting ENTRYPOINT to planeon_maint_t passes check_matrix and all 206 assertions. The same holds for planeon_etc_t recategorised to ENTRYPOINT for planeon_maint_t, and for qualk8s_datastore_data_t recategorised to CONTAINER_FILE for planeon_admin_t. The interpreter recategorised and granted to planeon_server_t is caught (A60.49.entrypoint). Candidate 4's A77.planeon_interpreter_exec_t would have failed in the first case. check_matrix does not tie the ENTRYPOINT or CONTAINER_FILE category to particular types. A recategorisation is a visible change to a type row, so this is defence in depth, not an open route.
findings.requiredChange: Optional. Restore A77.planeon_interpreter_exec_t (it can fail, so it is not vacuous) with a two-op mutation, or have check_matrix fix the ENTRYPOINT category to the sixteen declared exec types and CONTAINER_FILE to qualk8s_container_file_t.
